messages:
Sam (VP Eng): Quick follow-up from today's All-Hands Q&A : major releases move to a biweekly window, minors and hotfixes remain flexible. How do we operationalize this for oncall and quality gates?
Iris (Release Eng): Suggest we add 'release_type' and 'freeze_date' to the ticket template and require an ops owner for majors. I'll update the template.
Noah (SRE): For majors: canary >=4h, staged ramp plan, and a 48h post-rollout watch. Auto-create incident if error_rate > 0.4% or p99 > baseline*1.3.
Faye (QA): QA gates for majors: critical tests 100% green, smoke pass, and regression delta <3% on top-200 prompts. I'll publish a short checklist and add a sample command.
Jordan (Eng Ops): I'll draft customer-facing wording: 72h heads-up for majors, optional opt-out for Dedicated customers. Also create a one-page runbook for release-day oncall tasks.
Priya (Product): Need a clear definition of 'major' for PMs. Proposal: any change to public API, storage schema, billing, or infra components = major. Agree?
Sam (VP Eng): Leadership agrees with that definition. One more ask: keep hotfix path simple and fast. Ops + Release + QA to finalize checklist by EOW so we can pilot next window.
deploy-bot: "Canary scheduled: 10% at 15:00 UTC. Monitoring p95/p99 and error-rate. Rollback thresholds set."
Iris (Release Eng): I'll post updated ticket JSON and a minimal checklist in Confluence and schedule a 30m sign-off on Friday.
Faye (QA): Quick copyable snippet for checklist: ```
python eval/run.py --prompts top200.txt --baseline baseline.json --cand build_789 --max_regression 0.03
```
I'll link the full harness after review.
Jordan (Eng Ops): Owners: Jordan (customer comms + runbook), Iris (ticket template + release flow), Faye (QA checklist), Noah (monitoring + rollback rules), Priya (PM guidance). Closing thread ; will post RFC draft here later.
